clue.text: Playwright cut short in awkward act? One completes work quickly

indicators.note: something cut short loses its tail, so the dramatist's name drops its final letter
an awkward arrangement is a clumsy, disordered one, so these three letters get jumbled
one element is placed inside the other, the name going into the jumbled letters

blocks.note: first letter of the jumbled word act
Clifford Odets, the American dramatist of Waiting for Lefty
remaining letters of the jumbled word act

explanation.surface: A dramatist's play is trimmed into a clumsy act, then someone races to finish a piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Clifford Odets was an American playwright. A codetta is a brief coda, so it rounds off a musical work in short order.
explanation.definitionFit: A codetta is a short concluding passage in music, a small coda that brings a movement or section swiftly to its close.

clue.text: Public school (not amateur), good in social standing – it raises the blood!

indicators.note: not means without, so the word for an amateur is taken away from the school's name
in places the preceding letters inside the word for social standing

blocks.note: Uppingham is a public (fee-paying) school in Rutland
a ham is an amateur, especially a radio enthusiast or poor actor
G is the abbreviation for good
class is one's social rank

explanation.surface: A posh school, minus the dilettantes, ranks well socially, and something gets the blood racing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is an old private boarding school, such as Uppingham. 'Raises the blood' is literal: the device draws blood to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupping glass is heated and placed on the skin so the vacuum inside draws blood toward the surface, an old medical treatment.

clue.text: Added sound died round WWI battlefield mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the battlefield's name loses its final letter
round means surrounding, so the abbreviation for died wraps the battlefield

blocks.note: ob. is short for obiit, Latin for 'he died', seen on gravestones
Verdun saw a long, bloody battle in 1916

explanation.surface: Someone killed in the fighting around a Great War battle site, with an extra noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdub is to record extra sound over an existing recording, so overdubbed sound has been added afterwards.

clue.text: Klutz we chucked in bottom up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom to the top
chucked in means thrown inside, so the pronoun is put within the other word

blocks.note: the bottom of a river or sea is its bed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy person threw us in, landing us bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Klutz and dweeb are both American slang for a socially inept, awkward or foolish person.

clue.text: Winning means a lot to them – one score’s bitter stuff

definitions.text: Winning means a lot to them

blocks.note: a try is a score in rugby
ers is bitter vetch, a fodder plant

explanation.surface: Competitors who care about victory, and the sour taste of a single scoring play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like twenty or a game tally; here it is a rugby score. Ers is a dictionary name for the bitter vetch plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tryers are people who make an effort, earnest competitors for whom winning matters.

clue.text: Poet’s change in form, smart, new, recast

indicators.note: to recast is to mould again, so these letters are poured into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet's transformation of form, made smart and new by refashioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' marks an old poetic word: Spenser used transmew for transmute.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmew is Spenser's form of transmute, meaning to change something into a different form or nature.

clue.text: One of the hairtails kept in fyke on surface after bringing up

indicators.note: kept in means held within the following words, the letters lying inside them
in a down clue, bringing up means lifting the letters so they read upward

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: A fish caught in a fyke, a bag-net, sits on the surface after being hauled up.
explanation.walkthrough: A fyke is a bag net for fish, so the surface is all angling.
explanation.definitionFit: The snoek is a long, slender food fish of southern waters belonging to the hairtail family, the cutlassfishes.

clue.text: On the rocks? I give in (well, almost)

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the final letter of the yielding word is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
to cede is to give in or yield

explanation.surface: Someone tempted by a drink served over ice admits defeat, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' is filler in the surface, part of the parenthetical hesitation; 'almost' trims CEDE to CED.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink served on the rocks is poured over ice cubes, so it is chilled with frozen water.

clue.text: One not often badly brought up in tub and rarely innocent (happily)

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means turned to read upward
in places the turned word inside the word for a tub

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a dan is a tub or truck used in coal mines
illy is a rare adverb meaning badly

explanation.surface: Someone who seldom misbehaved was raised in a bathtub and is rarely guilty of anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not often' labels the word as rare, not as a frequency; DAN is a mining word for a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: Idyllian is a rare variant of idyllic, describing the happy innocence of a pastoral idyll.

clue.text: What’s mostly powdered up creating striking effect

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: talced means dusted with talcum powder

explanation.surface: Something largely dusted with powder gives a dramatic effect, like stage make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliance of effect or a showy, impressive success, from the French for a burst or flash.

clue.text: Realistic drama’s opening scene with drilling of teeth

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
drilling puts soldiers through manoeuvres, moving them into new positions, so these letters shift

blocks.note: first letter of drama
the five letters reordered
dental means relating to teeth

explanation.surface: A gritty drama opens with a scene of dental drilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drilling' fits the dental surface, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlyle coined descendental as the opposite of transcendental, meaning down-to-earth and concerned with the actual world.

clue.text: Conflict spread, a game of chance – guarantee in auld Scotland

blocks.note: war is armed conflict
as a stain or colour ran, it spread
dice is a gambling game

explanation.surface: War spreads, and fate rests on a throw of the dice, while the old Scots want a guarantee.
explanation.definitionFit: Warrandice is the old term in Scots law for a warranty or security given to protect a buyer's title.

clue.text: Wi’ water nan’s wee pride and joy damped firework he made?

definitions.text: Wi’ water nan’s wee pride and joy damped firework he made?

blocks.note: pee is urine, water in the bodily sense
oy (or oe) is Scots for a grandchild, a grandmother's little darling

explanation.surface: Granny's little grandson wet a firework with his own pee and so made a peculiar squib.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a peeoy is a home-made Scottish firework of damp gunpowder, and the clue jokes that the child dampened it in the most childish way.
explanation.definitionFit: Children in Scotland made a peeoy by moistening a small cone of gunpowder, which then fizzes and sparks when lit.

clue.text: Top family (top or backward)

indicators.note: backward means read in the opposite direction, from the end to the start

blocks.note: to top someone is slang for killing them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note about the highest-ranking family, with a puzzling aside about being on top or behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'top' is a verb, to kill, not the adjective it echoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the royal family, collectively called the royals, sit at the top of the social hierarchy.

clue.text: Seen being evasive in response after parking, intentionally

indicators.note: evasive movement dodges about, so these letters are shifted into another order
placed inside, so the jumbled letters go within the word for an answer
comes after means the larger chunk follows the parking abbreviation

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a reply is a response
the four letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone dodges in a reply after leaving the car, and does so on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Prepense survives mainly in the legal phrase malice prepense, malice planned in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepense means planned beforehand, as in malice prepense, so acting prepensely is doing something deliberately and with forethought.

clue.text: Electrical supply system: bookie has one installed (8, two words)

indicators.note: installed means fitted inside, so the numeral goes within the word for the bookie

blocks.note: a ringman is a bookmaker at the racecourse ring
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bookmaker gets a wiring system fitted at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring main is a domestic wiring circuit in which sockets are connected in a loop back to the supply.

clue.text: Fish found round Loch, bluish-grey locally?

indicators.note: something found round another surrounds it, so the fish word encloses the abbreviation

blocks.note: a skate is a flat ray-like fish
L is the map abbreviation for loch

explanation.surface: A fish turns up near a Scottish lake, coloured a dull blue-grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' marks a dialect word: sklate is the Scots spelling of slate, the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sklate is the Scots form of slate, and slate as a colour is a dull bluish grey like roofing stone.

clue.text: Feed rising in demand that can be filled

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read going upward
in means placed inside the word for demand

blocks.note: to bait a horse is to feed it
goods in demand have a sale

explanation.surface: Appetite grows for food, a demand that can be satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiable means capable of being satisfied or sated, so a satiable appetite can be filled up.

clue.text: Specialist collector: what’s mint is a must, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means this is only one way the letters might go, inviting another order

blocks.note: eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: For a dedicated collector, mint condition is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: coin collectors prize pieces in mint state, and a mint is where coins are struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A numismatist studies and collects coins and medals, a specialised field of collecting.

clue.text: Gnarled root’s position revealing type of palm

indicators.note: something gnarled is twisted and knotted, so these letters get twisted

blocks.note: the four letters twisted
the lie of something is its position

explanation.surface: Where a knotty root lies shows what sort of palm tree it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Troolie, or troelie, is the bussu palm of tropical America, whose huge leaves are used for thatching.

clue.text: The northern boy, Irish inside, going after maid, no grand landowner (11, two words)

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation within the word for a youngster
going after means the following chunks come behind the word for a maid

blocks.note: a bonne is a French maidservant
t' is the clipped form of 'the' in northern English dialect
a lad is a boy
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A northern lad of Irish blood follows a housemaid around, though he owns no great estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The northern' reads like a description of the boy, but it is the dialect form of the word itself, as in Yorkshire's 'down t' pit'. A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet laird was a small Scottish landowner who farmed his own land, wearing a bonnet like a commoner rather than a hat.

clue.text: Girl is making milky drinks

blocks.note: a lass is a girl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl is preparing yoghurt drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassi is an Indian drink of yoghurt or buttermilk blended with water, served sweet or salty.

clue.text: A trifle, as in ‘rotten wage’

indicators.note: rotten things fall apart and decay, so these letters break up and reform

blocks.note: e.g., for example, means 'as in'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor wage is dismissed as a pittance, a mere trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: A geegaw, more often spelt gewgaw, is a showy trinket or bauble of little value.

clue.text: Hide without outer covering? Not difficult formerly

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, the word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: leather is tanned hide

explanation.surface: An animal skin with its outer layer removed, which was once easy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb; it is the noun, an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Eathe is an archaic word meaning easy, so it describes something that was formerly not hard.

clue.text: Silver-cased tuning peg for taking off

indicators.note: something cased is enclosed in a covering, so the silver symbol wraps the peg

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a pin is a peg on a stringed instrument around which a string is wound

explanation.surface: A silver-covered tuning peg on an instrument, ready to be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' suggests removal, but here it means mimicking.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone off means imitating or mimicking them, which is exactly what aping someone is.

clue.text: Flat? Comparatively smart Rue Rivoli houses

indicators.note: a street that houses something holds it inside, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the words

explanation.surface: Are the apartments on Paris's elegant Rue de Rivoli more chic than others?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' suggests an apartment, which the Paris street supports; it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean level or exactly straight, as in a true surface, so truer means more flat.

clue.text: Medicated plaster, doctored sample torn badly

indicators.note: doctored means tampered with, so these letters have been altered in order
badly suggests things in a mess, so the second word's letters are scrambled too

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical dressing, a sample that has been tampered with and badly ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: An emplastron, or emplastrum, is an old term for a medicated plaster spread on cloth and applied to the skin.

clue.text: In, but missing out on boundaries, receives one within reach

indicators.note: missing the boundaries means losing the letters at both edges
something that receives takes another thing inside it

blocks.note: a side that is in at cricket is batting
a means one

explanation.surface: A cricket side is in but failing to hit boundaries, yet takes a wicket within range.
explanation.walkthrough: BATTING loses B and G to give ATTIN, which takes A inside. The cricket boundaries in the surface are also the edge letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to reach or achieve it, arriving at it by effort.

clue.text: Canadian force creating low tension after abuse of USA

indicators.note: abuse mistreats and disorders, so the letters of the country are rearranged
after means the abbreviations follow the jumbled letters

blocks.note: the three letters jumbled
L is the abbreviation for low
T is the symbol for tension in physics

explanation.surface: Canada's military arm is under strain after America mistreats it.
explanation.walkthrough: A force is a waterfall in northern English dialect, not an army; sault is the Canadian word for a rapid or fall, as in Sault Ste Marie.
explanation.definitionFit: In Canada a sault is a waterfall or rapid, and force is a northern English word for a waterfall.

clue.text: ‘Impaler’ includes strange line reminiscent of hallowed spot

indicators.note: strange means odd or unfamiliar, so the four letters appear in an unfamiliar order
something that includes another holds it within itself

blocks.note: the shrike, or butcher-bird, impales its prey on thorns
the four letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A note about a historical impaler and a weird line that recalls a sacred place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impaler' in quotes suggests Vlad the Impaler, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine is a holy place, so something shrinelike resembles or evokes such a sacred site.

clue.text: Wherein one’s cast with start of netting

definitions.text: Wherein one’s cast with start of netting

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: the sea is where a fishing line or net is cast
first letter of netting

explanation.surface: A riddle about the place where an angler casts, along with the beginnings of a net.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: to sean is to fish with a seine net, casting it in the sea. Sean is a variant spelling of seine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean is a variant of seine, a large dragnet, and as a verb means to fish by casting such a net.

clue.text: Predator ay leaving to rove aboard ship

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so those two letters go out of the wandering word
aboard a ship means inside it, so the remainder goes within the vessel word

blocks.note: taken as written: the letters removed
to stray is to wander or rove
keel stands for a ship by synecdoche, as in poetry

explanation.surface: A hunter says yes to leaving its roaming and climbs aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ay' looks like an exclamation of assent, but it is just the two letters to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon that hovers before swooping on mice and voles, a bird of prey.
